- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight mean reversion but don’t overshoot.  
- If recent price action shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce forecast momentum by 10–15% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), forecast should not exceed +3% above peak for next 3–5 days — cap upward momentum.  
- If sentiment is rising but price is falling, model should not overreact — forecast should lag sentiment by 1–2 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 5+ days), reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period — avoid “overfitting” to recent highs.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and price is trending sideways, forecast should be conservative — avoid sharp directional moves.
